title: SEC1: PinnedCertVerifier bypasses expiry/key validation
description: crates/kith-peer/src/lib.rs:433-436. PinnedCertVerifier::verify_server_cert accepts any cert that byte-matches the pinned DER without checking expiry, key usage, or verifying the TLS signature on the handshake with that cert's public key. The function is pub and named new_with_root_cert, not new_for_test — a maintainer may reach for it expecting real validation semantics. Risk: if the test cert format changes (e.g. regenerated with different encoding), the byte comparison silently fails instead of failing cleanly at cert parse time. Also: an attacker-replayed expired cert would pass if they held the DER bytes. Acceptable for test-only use, but the pub API surface and lack of a doc note saying 'never use in production' (which exists on new_with_root_cert but not on PinnedCertVerifier itself) creates confusion.
